image.subsector: Wireless towers and edge digital infrastructure
image.description: Mexico Telecom Partners, legally Mexico Tower Partners, S.A.P.I. de C.V., is a neutral Mexican digital-infrastructure platform that owns and operates towers, rooftop sites, distributed antenna systems, small cells, edge facilities and data-center infrastructure. The platform serves major wireless operators and colocation users across Mexico. It was formed in May 2014 by combining Digital Bridge and Macquarie Mexican Infrastructure Fund portfolios. A June 2026 BMV filing reported approximately 3,737 sites and confirmed an unchanged 50/50 ownership split: DigitalBridge through MTP Mexico Holding B.V., and Macquarie Asset Management through MMIT I and MMIT II. The 2022 Macquarie-side transfer was internal, InfraBridge is not a direct owner, and no signed or closed direct platform sale was identified through August 19, 2026.

image.name: Switch, Inc.
image.description: Switch, Inc. develops, owns and operates large-scale U.S. data-center campuses serving AI, cloud and enterprise customers. The platform was founded in 2000 and is headquartered in Las Vegas, with campuses in Nevada, Texas, Michigan and Georgia and a Pennsylvania expansion announced in 2026. DigitalBridge Partners II and IFM Global Infrastructure Fund completed the take-private on December 6, 2022. The latest comparable ownership schedule reports DigitalBridge at 55.8%, IFM at 37.2% and the management rollover group at 7.0%. Aware Super is also a current co-investor, but its exact stake, vehicle, closing date and nesting are not publicly disclosed and are not additive to that schedule. InfraBridge is not a direct owner, and no later signed or closed direct Switch transfer was identified through August 19, 2026.

image.name: Anza Renewables
image.description: Anza Renewables is the operating brand of Anza RE, LLC, a U.S. software-enabled procurement, data and analytics platform serving solar and battery-storage developers, independent power producers and other energy buyers. Its tools support module, inverter, storage and transformer sourcing, supplier evaluation and purchase-order execution. The business formally launched from Borrego in September 2022. Borrego contracted to sell all Anza RE, LLC equity to Anza RE Buyer, LLC on February 24, 2023 for US$26.74 million, and Anza announced the completed separation on May 17, 2023 with investment from ECP's Energy Transition Opportunities Fund, Angeleno Group and other investors. ECP and Angeleno continue to list Anza as active; exact stakes, control, the full cap table and the legal closing day are not publicly disclosed. The company is headquartered in Oakland, California and reports more than 80 subscribers and support for over 8 GW of PV and 5 GWh of BESS purchase orders. No later sale or signed pending exit was identified through August 19, 2026.

image.name: Braya Renewable Fuels
image.subsector: Renewable diesel and low-carbon fuels refining
image.description: Braya Renewable Fuels is the manager-level renewable-fuels platform operating the Come By Chance refinery in Newfoundland and Labrador through Braya Renewable Fuels (Newfoundland) LP. Cresta Fund Management acquired control in November 2021, while Silverpeak-managed North Atlantic Refining Corp. retained a minority interest. ECP announced a US$300 million preferred-equity investment in April 2023. Exact sponsor percentages, voting rights and holding vehicles are not publicly disclosed, and ECP Fund V is not directly supported for this investment. Commercial renewable-diesel operations began in February 2024; after a temporary 2025 shutdown, operations resumed, and the platform announced its first 100,000-barrel Canadian renewable-diesel sale in June 2026. Braya serves fuel markets in Canada, the United States, Mexico and Europe, while sustainable aviation fuel and green hydrogen or ammonia remain planned rather than confirmed commercial products. No later sale, sponsor exit or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 19, 2026.

image.name: Arium Networks
aliases: Crown Castle Small Cell & Venue business
image.description: Arium Networks LLC is a U.S. small-cell, distributed-antenna-system and venue-network infrastructure platform created from Crown Castle's former Small Cell business. It designs, deploys and manages outdoor and in-building wireless networks for the three largest U.S. mobile network operators and venue customers. EQT Active Core Infrastructure I announced the acquisition in March 2025 and completed it through Small Cells HoldCo Inc. on May 1, 2026, when Arium launched as a standalone company. Arium reported more than 100,000 small cells on air or under contract across 43 states at launch and is headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina. EQT continues to list Arium as current. The separately sold Crown Castle Fiber Solutions business now owned by Zayo is outside this company boundary. Public sources do not disclose one comparable EQT economic stake across the nested fund and co-investment structure, and no later platform sale, sponsor exit or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 29, 2026.

image.name: EdgeConneX
image.description: EdgeConneX is a global data-center developer and operator headquartered in Herndon, Virginia. Founded in 2009, it develops and operates edge, hyperscale, purpose-built and build-to-density facilities for hyperscale, cloud, enterprise, content, network, technology and AI customers. Public materials describe more than 80 operating or developing sites across over 60 markets in more than 20 countries, with over 10 GW of additional planned capacity. EQT Infrastructure IV completed the Providence-led acquisition on November 5, 2020; EQT Infrastructure V joined in 2021, Sixth Street-managed funds completed a minority investment in 2024, and EQT AI Infrastructure acquired a minority interest from EQT Infrastructure IV and V in 2026 while EQT remained the largest shareholder group. Liberty Global fully exited its former minority interest on June 29, 2026. CPP Investments' $1.75 billion commitment supports EQT's broader AI infrastructure strategy but is not disclosed as a separate direct EdgeConneX shareholding. Individual sites, campuses, subsidiaries, AdaniConneX and Chayora are outside this canonical company boundary. No later company sale, EQT exit, Sixth Street exit or signed pending ownership transfer was identified through August 29, 2026.

image.description: Montecito Medical Outpatient Portfolio is the bounded 2025 Project Lotus sale-recapitalization of a national medical-outpatient portfolio. image.name: CleanCapital Holdings, LLC
image.description: CleanCapital Holdings, LLC develops, acquires, owns and operates distributed solar and energy-storage projects across the United States. Founded in 2015 and headquartered in New York, the platform serves commercial, industrial, institutional, utility and public-sector counterparties through contracted clean-energy assets. Generate Capital and CleanCapital established a project-acquisition warehouse in 2017 targeting approximately US$300 million of operating clean-energy assets; this was project-level financing and ownership rather than disclosed corporate equity, and Generate's exact project stake and exit date were not publicly disclosed. BlackRock Renewable Power Group funds made a direct corporate investment in 2019, but that period is historical. Manulife Investment Management made a corporate investment in 2021 through Manulife Infrastructure Fund II and remains the only named current institutional backer. The exact Manulife and former BlackRock percentages are not publicly disclosed. Infranity's January 2026 capital is a holdco debt facility, and no platform sale or signed ownership exit was identified through August 29, 2026.

image.name: ACES Delta, LLC
image.description: ACES Delta, LLC is a clean-hydrogen production and underground salt-cavern storage platform in Delta, Utah. The 2019 joint venture is currently owned by Chevron-controlled Magnum Development, LLC as majority owner and Mitsubishi Power Americas, Inc. as minority owner; exact percentages are not publicly disclosed. Haddington Energy Partners III formerly owned the platform indirectly through Magnum and exited that position when Chevron acquired 100% of Magnum in 2023. Haddington ESP I separately manages construction equity in the ACES I project company, while GIC, Ontario Teachers', AIMCo and Manulife are investors in that fund rather than verified direct ACES Delta owners. The first stage comprises 220 MW of electrolysis and two salt caverns supporting more than 300 GWh of storage. All 40 electrolyzers were reported commissioned in the first quarter of 2026, with final start-up still expected later in 2026. No later platform sale or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 29, 2026.

milestones.event: Magnum Development and Mitsubishi Hitachi Power Systems announced the Advanced Clean Energy Storage joint venture that became ACES Delta.
The U.S. Department of Energy closed a US$504.4 million loan guarantee for the ACES I hydrogen-production and storage project; the facility is debt rather than equity ownership.

Haddington announced US$650 million of commitments to Haddington ESP I from GIC, Ontario Teachers', AIMCo and Manulife; the institutions invested as fund LPs, not as disclosed direct ACES Delta owners.
Chevron acquired 100% of Magnum Development from Haddington, obtaining a majority interest in ACES Delta; Mitsubishi Power Americas remained the minority joint-venture owner.
HydrogenPro reported that all 40 electrolyzers comprising the 220 MW first stage had been commissioned, while final project start-up remained expected in the second half of 2026.
